case_prompt: A 31-year-old man with no history of atopy or chronic illness presented with sudden-onset, intensely pruritic skin lesions. He denied fevers, arthralgias, muscle weakness, or recent medication use. On examination, there were erythematous to violaceous linear streaks in a flagellate pattern symmetrically over his arms and legs, coalescing over his chest and scalp. Discrete pustules were noted on his trunk and in intertriginous areas; there was no mucosal involvement. He reported eating partially cooked shiitake mushrooms 10 days before presentation and consuming raw shiitake mushrooms 6 days later. The rash appeared 24 hours after the raw-mushroom exposure. Complete blood count and liver and renal function tests were within normal limits. A skin biopsy showed follicular sterile pustules with a mild mixed perivascular inflammatory infiltrate.

sentences.text: A 31-year-old man with no history of atopy or chronic illness presented with sudden-onset, intensely pruritic skin lesions.
He denied fevers, arthralgias, muscle weakness, or recent medication use.
On examination, there were erythematous to violaceous linear streaks in a flagellate pattern symmetrically over his arms and legs, coalescing over his chest and scalp.
Discrete pustules were noted on his trunk and in intertriginous areas; there was no mucosal involvement.
He reported eating partially cooked shiitake mushrooms 10 days before presentation and consuming raw shiitake mushrooms 6 days later.
The rash appeared 24 hours after the raw-mushroom exposure.
Complete blood count and liver and renal function tests were within normal limits.
A skin biopsy showed follicular sterile pustules with a mild mixed perivascular inflammatory infiltrate.

diagnostic_reasoning: 1. Dermatomyositis was considered but excluded by the absence of systemic manifestations such as muscle involvement or constitutional symptoms [“He denied any systemic symptoms or exposure to medication.”]. 2. Docetaxel-induced flagellate dermatitis was considered but excluded by the patient’s lack of any chemotherapy history [“He denied any systemic symptoms or exposure to medication.”].

selection.screen_reason: Pruritic flagellate dermatitis a day after eating raw shiitake, with no drugs or systemic disease, is classic shiitake dermatitis and needs a good exposure history.
selection.second_look_note: Eating raw shiitake 24 hours before flagellate dermatitis is the decisive history clue.
